thread.title: This 'dangerous trade' is making a comeback and that is a worry for stocks: Saxo Bank

author: morningstar.com
title: This 'dangerous trade' is making a comeback and that is a worry for stocks: Saxo Bank
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
As we near the finish line of a long week in politics, the Fed is swinging back on the radar for investors.
Minutes published by the central bank on Wednesday, which showed a September rate increase is firmly on the cards (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-minutes-show-support-for-september-interest-rate-hike-combined-with-anxiety-about-a-trade-war-2018-08-22), have helped distract from some legal heat circling former Trump advisers. Jackson Hole here we come (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/jackson-hole-guards-the-secrets-of-the-temple-2018-08-22).
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/jackson-hole-guards-the-secrets-of-the-temple-2018-08-22)Those Fed musings also took a bit of steam out of the S&P 500, something that could continue this morning as the buck stomps ahead. And it could muddy the waters for those wondering whether to dive into the longest bull market on record.
Our call of the day, from Saxo Bank's Peter Garnry, advises opting opt for the latter strategy as he warns of a "dangerous trade" that's been making a comeback, and which he says could blindside the market.
He says investors have been buying stocks and pushing the S&P 500 to new highs while paying "record premium" for hedging against downside risk in the index via the Cboe SKEW Index . That's shown in the following chart:
"The most popular ETN engaging in shorting short-term VIX futures is up 25% from its April lows," said Garnry, in a follow-up email to a recent webinar (https://www.tradingfloor.com/posts/equity-update-webinar-new-highs-in-sp-500-9673509?int_cmpid=TF_email_trader_i_follow_posts_video) where he laid out those concerns.
He says this structure was in place during all of 2017--notable moments are here (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wall-streets-fear-index-bounces-off-23-year-low-as-tech-stocks-sink-2017-06-09) and here (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/a-popular-wall-street-stock-market-black-swans-gauge-is-at-a-record-level-2017-03-20)--and then earlier this year. "It is a big worry for me that we are back to this market structure again...with the U.S. equity market having outperformed massively all other markets on top of compressed implied volatility," says Garnry.
He says it "sets the stage for a violent drop in U.S. equities should we get some exogenous shock to the system."
One alternative? Emerging markets.
Garnry acknowledges that emerging markets have lots of structural issues, but maintains they can still yield attractive returns. To be sure, there are plenty of emerging-markets haters out there, which some could be a reason to dive in (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/time-to-buy-emerging-markets-and-seven-stocks-and-funds-to-consider-2018-08-23). Don't count Deutsche Bank in that camp. They've got a laundry list of reasons why it is too soon to seek out those far-flung stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stocks-have-trounced-emerging-markets-this-year-and-deutsche-bank-doesnt-expect-that-to-change-2018-08-22).
Key market gauges
Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures are straddling the flat line this morning. That is after the S&P and Dow snapped a four-day winning streak Wednesday as after those heavy Fed hints over a rate increase next month (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-minutes-show-support-for-september-interest-rate-hike-combined-with-anxiety-about-a-trade-war-2018-08-22).
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-minutes-show-support-for-september-interest-rate-hike-combined-with-anxiety-about-a-trade-war-2018-08-22)Read more in Market Snapshot (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-futures-flat-as-investors-digest-fed-minutes-2018-08-23)
Elsewhere, Asia stocks generally rose (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-wrestle-between-gains-and-losses-2018-08-22) even as fresh U.S. and China tariffs kick in, while Europe stocks are up modestly (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-shares-tick-higher-but-bank-stocks-lower-2018-08-23). Oil prices are edging back from a two-week peak (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-oil-edges-back-from-2-week-peak-but-tighter-supplies-remain-an-issue-2018-08-23), while gold is off.
The dollar is up (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-rises-after-six-day-drop-pound-south-african-rand-soften-2018-08-23), notably against the South African rand , which is taking a big hit after Trump tweeted about the country's land- seizure crisis:
(https://twitter.com/realDonaldTrump/status/1032454567152246785)
Bitcoin has taken a tumble overnight after the SEC shot down nine bitcoin-based ETF applications. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sec-again-shoots-down-bitcoin-based-etf-applications-2018-08-22)
The chart
Wolf Richter of the Wolf Street has hawks on his mind as he takes a deep dive into the Fed minutes. He discovered the central bank used the word "strong" 32 times at its most recent meeting, a 150% increase on a year earlier and maybe the most ever for a set of minutes.
"Even in 2005, during the first half of the rate-hike cycle at the time, when the Fed was gung-ho about the economy, the word "strong" appeared between 3 times and 9 times in the minutes," says Richter.
So he stacked that up against some history, and, voilà, the following chart, which he advises to take with several grains of salt, explained fully in his blog (https://wolfstreet.com/2018/08/22/the-feds-hawkishness-spikes-according-to-my-chart/).
The stat
62.5%--that is how much Chinese imports of sorghum dropped in July (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/08/23/reuters-america-china-july-grains-imports-fall-sharply-after-u-s-tariffs.html)versus a year ago, after the government slapped hefty tariffs on grains coming into the country in retaliation for U.S. action. On Thursday, more tariffs by both countries kicked in as scheduled. Meanwhile, reps from each side meet in Washington this week to find a solution to the long-running spat
The buzz
Chinese tech giant Alibaba (BABA) is in the earnings spotlight this morning, with results that just rolled out (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/alibabas-stock-surges-after-revenue-and-adjusted-profit-rises-but-comes-up-shy-of-views-2018-08-23). Hormel (HRL) is down as sales fall short and its outlook gets cut (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/hormel-foods-stock-falls-after-sales-come-up-shy-outlook-lowered-2018-08-23).
Gap (GPS) , HP (HPQ), Intuit (INTU) and VMware (VMW) will also report.
Saudi Arabia says it isn't scrapping plans (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/saudi-arabia-denies-canceling-aramco-ipo-but-suggests-delay-report-2018-08-22) for an IPO of state-owned energy giant Aramco, but may delay it.
Facebook (FB) will pull its data-security app Onavo (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-to-yank-onavo-data-security-app-from-apple-store-2018-08-22) from Apple's (AAPL) app store after the latter claimed it violated data-collection rules. And another 4 million users (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-says-another-4-million-users-may-have-had-data-misused-2018-08-22) may have had their data misused, says the social media giant.
AT&T (T) is betting viewers will pay to watch a $9 million match (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/att-bets-golf-fans-will-pay-to-watch-tiger-woods-vs-phil-mickelson-2018-08-22) between the golfing legends over Thanksgiving.
Is a no-deal Brexit on the way? Here's what investors need to think about. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gear-up-for-a-no-deal-brexit-5-areas-to-watch-2018-08-22)
Random reads
All that stood between Paul Manafort and 18 convictions was a single juror (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/lone-holdout-juror-prevented-manafort-from-being-found-guilty-on-all-counts-report-2018-08-22)
Unable to evacuate, Hawaiians hunker down for a Cat. 4 hurricane (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/as-hurricane-lane-pushes-toward-hawaii-heres-what-travelers-need-to-know-2018-08-22)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/as-hurricane-lane-pushes-toward-hawaii-heres-what-travelers-need-to-know-2018-08-22)Cluster of 'Ring of fire' earthquakes raise fears of the "Big One" hitting California (https://nypost.com/2018/08/22/ring-of-fire-hit-with-70-earthquakes-in-just-48-hours/)
(https://www.gulflive.com/news/index.ssf/2018/08/unable_to_evacuate_hawaii_resi.html)Famed Ohio State football coach suspended over mishandling abuse allegations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ohio-state-coach-urban-meyer-suspended-for-3-games-over-mishandled-domestic-abuse-case-2018-08-22)
Best-selling band of all times in Kansas? One guess (https://mapsontheweb.zoom-maps.com/post/177132680547/the-best-selling-artist-or-band-from-each-state)
